summary: Most visitors need Gabon’s official e-Visa, applied for online through the DGDI portal and collected on arrival at Libreville’s Léon-Mba International Airport, while CEMAC citizens enter freely and several Western nationalities have been granted visa-free entry under measures announced in late 2023.

notes: Exporting ivory, wildlife trophies or protected animal and plant products is prohibited without CITES permits.
Large amounts of CFA franc cash are subject to BEAC currency-control rules. Declare significant sums on arrival and departure.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at larger hotels and supermarkets in Libreville and Port-Gentil, but Gabon is overwhelmingly a cash economy. Carry CFA francs, especially outside the main cities.

safety.text: Gabon is calmer than much of the region, but petty crime occurs in Libreville and Port-Gentil, and the political situation has been in transition since 2023. Avoid demonstrations and keep documents on you.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Gabon Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: The long dry season from late May to September is the best window for Loango and the national parks — cooler, drier and with easier road access.

tips.text: The e-Visa is only collected on arrival at Libreville Léon-Mba International Airport — if you plan to enter overland or through another port, arrange a visa through an embassy instead.
The yellow fever certificate is checked on arrival — travelers without a valid yellow card can be refused entry or vaccinated on the spot.
Withdraw CFA francs in Libreville before traveling — ATMs are scarce and unreliable outside the capital and Port-Gentil, and cards are rarely accepted upcountry.
Visits to Loango, Lopé and other national parks need advance planning — internal flights, boats and park guides are limited and best booked through a lodge or operator.
Avoid photographing government buildings, the port, airports and anything military. It can lead to questioning or confiscation of your camera.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Gabon?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. The standard route is Gabon’s official e-Visa (evisa.dgdi.ga), collected on arrival at Libreville airport. CEMAC citizens enter freely, and nationals of the US, Canada, the UK and EU countries have been covered by visa-exemption measures announced in late 2023 — implementation has varied, so confirm before travel.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Gabon?
faq.answer: Only with prior approval: e-Visa applicants receive an authorization online and the visa itself is issued on arrival, exclusively at Libreville Léon-Mba International Airport. There is no walk-up visa on arrival, and other entry points require a visa obtained from an embassy.

faq.question: Are US and EU citizens visa-free for Gabon?
faq.answer: Gabon’s transitional government announced visa exemptions for a list of countries including the US, Canada, the UK and EU members in late 2023 for short tourist stays. Reports of how it is applied at the border vary, so check with the DGDI portal or a Gabonese embassy shortly before traveling. The e-Visa remains a safe fallback.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Gabon?
faq.answer: Yes. Gabon requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from all travelers aged 1 year and over, regardless of where you are arriving from, and it is checked on arrival.

faq.question: What currency is used in Gabon?
faq.answer: The Central African CFA franc (XAF), shared with Cameroon, Congo, Chad, the Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea. Cash dominates outside the biggest hotels, so carry francs — euros are the easiest currency to exchange.
